# Spindle

> Spindle chooses, hands over, and tracks the skills coding agents use. A house
> keeps a short list of rules and kernel skills always on in every harness; a
> catalog of commit-pinned skills is searched and judged per task and handed over
> by path; every outcome is recorded against the skill. For skills that must be
> installed, an evidence-bearing lifecycle and control plane inspects, tries,
> verifies, and retires them with custody. Python CLI, MIT licensed. Spindle v0.4.

For the whole documentation in one file, read [bundle.md](bundle.md).

## Core idea

- The model picks worse from a longer skill list, so keep the always-on list
  short (the house kernel) and search the rest (the catalog) per task.
- `spindle house init <dir>` then `spindle house setup` installs house rules into
  `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, and `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` (managed
  blocks) and links kernel skills. `spindle house update` keeps a machine current.
  `spindle house setup --here --pattern <name>` vendors a project pattern.
- `catalog.toml` lists sources pinned to full commits, with optional `include`
  and `exclude` globs. `spindle catalog sync` indexes them without executing
  anything; `spindle catalog update <slug>` shows what a newer commit changes.
- `spindle find "<task>"` ranks catalog skills (full-text search, optional search
  expander, usage prior) and, with a judge (Jev, via `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`), selects
  those likely to materially help. `spindle use <source>/<name>` prints the
  SKILL.md path. `spindle report --outcome accepted|rejected --helped <ref>`
  records the result; `spindle usage` shows the record.
- Job runtimes call `spindle brief --json` before dispatch (`prompt_block`,
  `skills`, `selection`, `read_roots`) and `spindle report --selection --job`
  after grading. `SPINDLE_JOB` attributes the agent's own lookups. Sourcing never
  gates a job.
- For installed skills: inspect → try/borrow → compose → bootstrap → realize →
  activate → evaluate → adopt/update/distill/release/retire. `try` is one
  disposable session, `borrow` an expiring lease, and only `adopt` creates
  custody. `spindle harness setup --harness <codex|claude> --here` projects a
  small operator; it reads live state from `spindle harness context`.
- Install: `uv tool install "git+https://github.com/lavallee/spindle@v0.4.2"`, or
  the plugin from `lyra-forge/marketplace` (`claude plugin install
  spindle@lyra-forge`, `codex plugin add spindle@lyra-forge`).

## Pages

- [Overview](index.html): the house, the catalog, and judged per-task choice.
- [Why a small house](rationale.html): selection accuracy, and the costs of an
  unmanaged pile.
- [The house](house.html): rules, kernel, patterns, machine and project setup.
- [The catalog](catalog.html): sources and pins, find/use/report, the selection
  pipeline, feedback, job runtimes, trust.
- [The vetting lifecycle](lifecycle.html): inspect, try, borrow, adopt, update,
  retire.
- [How it works](how-it-works.html): record chain, composition, startup,
  rendering, safety floor.
- [Evaluation](evaluation.html): usage evidence versus paired held-out
  experiments.
- [Guide](guide.html): recipes and the CLI reference.
